Q1: Calcium cyanamide presents known hazards (Tier 1) for acute and chronic environmental effects, oral exposure, dermal and eye contact, and organ/systemic hazards. It also shows expanded perspective hazards (Tier 2) concerning carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards, and inhalation. Data on endocrine disruption hazards are currently deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Calcium cyanamide is listed as a Hazardous Air Pollutant and is included in the National Air Toxics Assessment, indicating recognized concerns regarding its presence in the atmosphere.
Q3: This chemical is well characterized, evidenced by over 6,000 literature references, a specific molecular formula (CH2N2.Ca), and a defined substance class. While there is a data deficiency for endocrine disruption hazards (one Tier 4 classification), it is not an incompletely defined UVCB substance.
